topIssues.title: fix(elizaos): reject unreadable migration sources before archive creation
topIssues.author: lalalune
topIssues.body:
## Problem and scope

OpenClaw optional filesystem helpers catch all read errors as missing data. A real unreadable SOUL.md plus readable MEMORY.md produces a normal migration source with missing persona and no warnings. Distinguish absent optional paths from unreadable or wrong-type existing paths and preserve causes.

## Acceptance and evidence

Real filesystem EACCES and wrong-type cases fail before CLI output artifacts; missing optional files remain supported. Preserve explicit SQLite compatibility warnings. Run owning package and root gates.

topIssues.title: fix(form): publish SQL-compatible component data envelopes
topIssues.author: lalalune
topIssues.body:
## Problem

A real FormService.startSession call with AgentRuntime and plugin-sql PGlite fails before persistence. The form serializer deliberately returns a null-prototype record; Drizzle inspects the top-level component data value and assumes a prototype. In-memory component fixtures did not exercise this boundary.

## Scope and acceptance

Preserve the safe public serializer and its own-key handling. Publish an adapter-compatible ordinary top-level JSON envelope for session, submission and autofill component writes, without invoking untrusted getters or changing nested values. Do not alter the general SQL adapter or public form lifecycle.

Verify actual FormService start/update/stash/restore/submission/autofill against real PGlite; inspect saved rows and adversarial own-key roundtrips. Include full form package tests/typecheck/lint and root verification. No schema migration or external integration is required.

Audited base b676280384b15df54204276e34bb8740db26936f. Found while independently validating #30757 with the real database boundary.

topIssues.title: fix(form): align evaluator eligibility and cancellation confirmation states
topIssues.author: lalalune
topIssues.body:
## Problem and scope

Stashed-only forms pass evaluator shouldRun but prepare requires an active session and throws. Ready high-effort forms persist cancellation confirmation but context exposes the flag only for active status, so provider incorrectly nudges submission. Remove stashed-only admission and preserve confirmation for eligible ready sessions.

## Acceptance and evidence

Exercise real FormService persistence and provider/evaluator: stash is ineligible, restore becomes eligible; ready high-effort cancellation asks confirmation, second explicit cancellation completes. Preserve normal active and low-effort behavior. Run full form tests/typecheck/lint, real-model evidence and root verify.

Audited base: b676280384b15df54204276e34bb8740db26936f. This is a confirmed second-pass cleanup finding with independent plan review. No production deployment, credential changes, or funded transactions are part of this scope.

topIssues.title: fix(elizaos): preserve executable template files during scaffolding
topIssues.author: lalalune
topIssues.body:
## Problem and scope

Rendering the shipped executable codesign wrapper changes mode 0755 to 0644. Generated Electrobun scripts prepend its directory to PATH, but command lookup bypasses the wrapper. Preserve source executable bits in the rendered output, consolidate identical publication logic and safely share the existing ignored-entry inventory.

## Acceptance and evidence

Run the real rendered wrapper through PATH with a controlled signing boundary; cover text/binary output and existing destinations. Build and pack the CLI, execute create/upgrade, owning tests/typecheck/lint and root verify.

topPRs.title: feat(cloud): reconcile subscription lifecycle and primary billing policy
topPRs.author: NubsCarson
topPRs.body:
Advances #23093, #23094 and #23095; also supplies the consent-bound registration prerequisite for #30638. These issues remain open. Pending hosted and live-integration acceptance.

# Behavior

Stripe terminal observations now publish lifecycle history, receipt, entitlement projection, policy generation and cancellation notice intent atomically. A failed write rolls back the whole transition. Historical event replay cannot restore older subscription authority.

Session-authorized managers can schedule and undo period-end cancellation. Commands record dispatch provenance before mutation and verify canonical Customer/subscription state before publication. Uncertain outcomes reconcile by retrieval without an automatic second mutation. Undo requires the captured schedule lineage to remain valid before dispatch. Tenant-scoped pending-command pagination exposes stale source identity and command uncertainty. Scheduling cancellation preserves current access until an effective terminal transition.

Existing-v1 paid renewal verifies the complete invoice, subscription, Customer, PaymentIntent, captured charge and catalog binding before granting allowance. Only a full captured, non-refunded, unadjusted monthly payment for an adjacent effective period can publish. Duplicate invoice/event delivery cannot grant twice. Unsupported observations retain retryable incident state.

Resource and inference admission use the same primary policy generation as billing snapshots. Cached paid state refreshes after a committed Free transition; missing or ambiguous required canonical authority is unavailable. Canonical-none non-subscriber accounts retain their existing legacy fallback. New allowance reservations and snapshot spendability share current organization/source/projection/period/grant identity checks. Denied spending is explicitly unavailable while ledger amounts remain intact; eligible exhausted allowance reports an observed zero. Historical reservations retain their settlement/refund ownership.

Generic app billing registration records owner and infrastructure-payer provenance and creates individual buyer accounts only after existing app consent. Merchant and subscription policy remain explicitly unconfigured. Cancellation notices have immutable identity, one durable attempt and distinct accepted/rejected/uncertain/unavailable outcomes. Dispatch requires server-approved per-revision recipients, content and delivery window. Missing policy does not send; uncertain SMTP acceptance does not trigger automatic resend or prove delivery.

The existing authenticated Stripe cron also recovers missed terminal observations using read-only canonical SDK requests. Durable leases, retry scheduling and complete-body deadlines bound provider work without retrying writes. Recovery publishes source/projection/generation/notice atomically and preserves webhook watermark provenance. Matching later events use a no-op only for a durably applied recovery revision with a coherent projection; ordinary webhook behavior is unchanged. Independent cron lanes retain failures and successful receipts separately.

# Validation and review

Current head `2d85438b7c8cd54a38227dd3376e10033a07e5d6`, rebased on `c2d55bf5e460055c19fb0c8bdfe217e4f1b2c8d8` (41 commits).

- Normal pinned install passed (Bun1.3.14 / Node24.15.0); private dependency paths verified after repairing three old local dependency links. Source unchanged.
- Current root verification:377/377 tasks, zero cache hits, all audits passed; single-worker Turbo9m21s, unchanged checkout.
- Current login/subscription checks:90 tests257 assertions passed, including manager authorization, commands and nonce exchange.
- Four current-head actual database captures passed and were inspected; complete records below.
- Prior full shared775e:12,801 passed243 skipped0failed81,637 assertions. Prior fullAPI775e:603 isolated files,6,514 passed4skipped0failed37,154 assertions. Prior post-inference-rebase suites127/502 passed. These remain historical receipts, not full-suite claims for this head.

Hosted failures from the initial revision were diagnosed and independently reviewed: seven fixed Stripe fixture sentinels now have an exact-path AND exact-line scanner exception (41-commit scan passes; changed literal and unlisted-path controls still fail); the PostgreSQL observer refreshes activity snapshots inside its transaction; two payment-replay assertions preserve every queue counter while accepting added cron lane receipts. At this head, [hosted PostgreSQL](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/actions/runs/34063750156/job/101568795230) passed 26 tests / 131 assertions across seven suites with no skips, including the formerly failing deletion/provisioning concurrency test. [Payment replay](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/actions/runs/34063750156/job/101568795420) passed its Chromium test: response-loss recovery, same-event and distinct-event deduplication, one $5 settlement, and rendered balance/invoice. This uses controlled Stripe, not live Stripe; no screenshots were captured. Windows security and Source static smoke also passed at this head. Static validation scanned all 41 commits without leaks, passed 138 workflow-contract tests, and completed affected lint (143/143), typecheck (234/234) and build (132/132). A subsequent fresh-develop merge check found two conflicts; rebase and new-head validation are pending.

Different authors reviewed lifecycle, commands, policy, snapshots, renewal, recovery, notices and the consolidated patch. Review found and fixed two composition defects: healthy unscheduled recovery degrading the cron, and cancel→undo→valid paid renewal preventing a later cancellation. Regression coverage retains corruption, missing-receipt, nonadjacent-period and provider-drift denials. Rebase conflict resolutions and the two final fixture repairs were independently reviewed. No production guard was relaxed to make fixtures pass.

Five large generated migration snapshots preserve reviewed generator provenance and a valid chain; most size is a full-schema metadata catch-up, not newly deployed tables. No captured evidence is committed.

# Remaining acceptance

Migrations0380–0385 add organization policy, registration, durable notices cancellation lineage and durable recovery receipts. This PR does not establish the proposed29/99 catalog, approved paid resource ceilings, generic trial/payer/access policy, Checkout/Portal, upgrades/downgrades, proration, other invoice outcomes or configured notice delivery.

Real signed Stripe/Test Clock, deployed two-user/Dedicated continuity and actual recipient observations remain separate requirements. No production migration, deployment or live provider billing/email operation is claimed. The supplied model-provider smoke is not billing evidence.

# Risks

Existing database migrations, encryption settings and persisted wire identifiers are deliberately preserved. # Background

## What does this PR do?

Own the login SDK and identity service as `@elizaos/login`. Replace external Steward package/source dependencies across desktop, Cloud and application consumers. Export React login components and wallet providers from the `@elizaos/ui` root barrel, with lazy wallet adapters and no `/login` package subpath. Remove unused trading/DeFi routes and SDK methods, the unreferenced trade-order/provider-action evaluators, their spend tracker and venue catalog; retain authentication, linking, MFA, recovery and required wallet contracts. Fix durable initialization, grant isolation, Node package resolution and graceful service shutdown. React logout now waits for access/refresh revocation and reports retryable failures; refresh revocation uses its verified tenant context. Correct IPv6 loopback parsing for HSTS. Configure a filtered Railpack deployment and resolve the shared error class from portable source in Cloudflare. Verify the standard migration ledger before startup, scope wallet provisioning and login audit writes to their tenant, and use one session verifier backed by the existing bootstrap authority query.

## What kind of change is this?

Feature and dependency migration with authentication correctness fixes.

topPRs.title: fix(cloud): preserve state and resource authority across lifecycle retries
topPRs.author: lalalune
topPRs.body:
This change preserves recoverable agent state and exact provider ownership across payment suspension, funded resume, replacement and deletion retries. A failed provider acknowledgement stays retryable. Cleanup uses the captured container, physical host and lifecycle generation, and cannot release a replacement host’s capacity or cancel deletion after teardown admission. Restored apps retain their configuration and credentials atomically, with outbound automation disabled.

The additional cleanup work retains a durable resource manifest covering compute, volumes, VPN and secrets. Ordinary replacement attempts now retain their placement and capacity authority before remote effects. A terminal or retried image job admits abandoned provider-success candidates into cleanup before releasing its execution binding. The existing daemon reconciles those records without treating lease expiry or missing acknowledgement as proof of absence. Recoverable volumes remain retained pending verified state recovery; compute absence alone does not authorize disk reclamation.

The exact restore provider additionally forces a quarantine marker into the container environment. In newly built images, the canonical shell entrypoint exits before normal startup when marked. A Linux/Docker counterfactual proved that the old script dispatched and wrote fixture state while the new one refused and left the candidate untouched. Historical images may lack this guard; image compatibility admission is still required. The provider-to-shell test and owning entrypoint tests passed.

The agent component work materializes a staged PGlite backup into an isolated candidate through the existing protected filesystem boundary. It checks the complete compressed digest, record order, archive paths and entry types; installs private files and directories; and persists/readbacks a replay-bound finish receipt. This does not open the production runtime, seal the cloud candidate, publish routing, or produce an activation MAC.

Tracks #23098, #22916, #20726 and #30746. This branch includes the earlier lifecycle work associated with the now-closed, unmerged prerequisite PRs #30714, #30745 and #30790.
